top_signals.title: Oil Prices Bounce Back Following Reports of U.S. Strikes on Iran
top_signals.summary: After shedding 7% yesterday, crude oil prices inched up earlier today following a Wall Street Journal report about a U.S. strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island. Brent crude traded at $105.26 per barrel at the time of writing, and West Texas Intermediate traded at $97.07 per barrel, after the WSJ cited unnamed U.S. officials as saying Iran’s Qeshm Island became a target in what they said was the latest in a series of “ limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out” over the past few weeks on Iran. Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
top_signals.summary: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructure. Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season and will be the largest storm system to make landfall in the region since Hurricane Helene in September 2024.
